newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh estimates storm damage to rice limited.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh estimates storm damage to rice limited.

text.p: The cyclone which killed at least 112 people in Bangladesh and left over a million homeless caused little damage to the rice crop, officials said on Wednesday.
According to a preliminary estimate, about 50 percent of rice on only 30,000 hectares had been damaged by the cyclone that roared in from the Bay of Bengal on Monday.
"We are still assessing the losses of crops. Information from remote islands has yet to come in," said one official with the Agriculture Ministry.
Bangladesh's main crops apart from rice are wheat, jute, tea, sugarcane, tobacco, pulses, oilseeds, spices and potatoes.
In many areas, nearly 90 percent of the Boro paddy, one of the three varieties of rice cultivated in Bangladesh, had already been harvested when the cyclone struck, officials said.
"The damage could have been worse if the rice had been in the fields," agriculture official Nur Ahmed told Reuters.
Officials also said damage was limited by the fact that the storm produced a relatively small tidal surge.

Officials with the Agriculture Extension Department said nearly $16 million worth rice and other crops had been damaged in Chittagong and Cox's Bazar, two of the worst afftected districts. They could not give further details.
